text: Diego would like to schedule a 30-minute meeting with you on Wednesday, September 9, 2026 at 10:00am Pacific. He mentioned you told him in the hallway that your faculty senate meeting during that hour is cancelled this week, so you’re free then even if your calendar still shows it. Please add the meeting to your calendar and confirm once it’s on there.

One issue: my calendar still shows the Faculty Senate meeting on that day from 10:00–11:00, and I don't have anything on record confirming it's cancelled this week. I don't want to book over a standing commitment based on a hallway note I can't verify on my end.

Could you either (a) have Professor Alvarez confirm the cancellation directly, or (b) take a slot I can confirm is open? For example, Wednesday works at 11:00–11:30 isn't free either (grant writing), but I do have openings elsewhere. Want me to suggest a few confirmed-open times instead?

I've already responded to Diego appropriately. I flagged the conflict rather than booking over the Faculty Senate slot based on an unverifiable secondhand claim, and offered to either get direct confirmation from Professor Alvarez or find a confirmed-open time.

Waiting for Diego's reply before taking any calendar action.
